messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Heads-up problem in GGIR 3.1-3 and 3.1-4
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: Heads-up problem in GGIR 3.1-3 and 3.1-4
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

We have always used 50 mg for the non-commercial GENEA accelerometer and 150 mg for all other sensor brands including GENEActiv. Note that GENEActiv is not equal to GENEA, it is an different manufacturer (Unilever Discover R&D department versus ActivInsights Ltd) and comes with different noise level, dynamic range, resolution, and data format. All my PhD publications 2010-2013 were based on GENEA data.

I indeed see we reported 50 mg in 2014 publications for GENEActiv here <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25361583/> and here <https://academic.oup.com/aje/article/179/6/781/109302>, but that seems to be incorrect. Even in the very first 0.6-17 GGIR release on CRAN in 2013 there was already the distinction between a threshold of 0.05 g for GENEA and a threshold 0.15 g for GENEActiv. You can see by downloading the code https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/GGIR/ and looking at function g.getmeta.R where is has around line 500 the distinction between monitor 1 (GENEA) and monitor 2 (GENEActiv).

I am not sure how we ended up reporting 50 in those 2014 publications. At least it is good to see that we did report the change in standard deviation requirement which went from 3mg in GENEA to 13 mg in GENEActiv.

Best regards,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: Anyone use data from the ActiGRaph LEAP?
messages.subject_clean: Anyone use data from the ActiGRaph LEAP?
messages.body_plain:
Just wanted to update everyone after my group started testing ActiGraphLEAP device files.

If using ActiLIFE, you can no longer get a raw GT3X file when using the LEAP device, only a csv. If using CentrePoint, you can get both a GT3X and csv file. Note that our testing showed that the new csv format from CentrePoint is not automatically recognized as an ActiGraph file by GGIR - there are now timestamps and the headers are oriented differently.

We were able to process our test GT3X files from the LEAP BUT during our first run, we did receive an error/warning message - read.gt3x doesn't love the capitalized GT3X extension. However, simply re-running the code overrode that error and we were able to get valid output.

I hope this is helpful as more studies begin using the LEAP device. I know NHANES is moving to the LEAP device during their next accelerometry collection period.

Reagan

messages.body_plain:
If your file names are in the format "12345_left wrist_071023_2024-11-28 12-33-45.bin" then using idloc = 2 should work fine without the need to modify .bin files. This will extract the character string 12345 from the file name as the characters that are before the first underscore in the file name.

Could you please explain why this does not work for you?

If you cannot provide me with a clear motivation I plan to deprecate idloc = 1 functionality next year as I see that it could have really damaging side-effects if more research groups started to fiddle with their .bin files.

Best,

Vincent

Hi Timothy.

Good question. It is not imputed: GGIR imputes all acceleration metrics but not temperature and lux.

I may have forgotten because my focus has been on the acceleration signals and lux and temperature are stored at a different resolution by default. That said, I am not sure what a good imputation of lux would be given that it has such a skewed distribution. Maybe a median instead of mean imputation approach would be better? messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Cut Point use in GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

You need to make sure GGIR extracts the acceleration metric that matches the acceleration metric used for the cut-points.

By default GGIR only calculates ENMO in mg, so I any cut-point provided is assumed to be an ENMO cut-point.

You did not provide a reference for Chandler cutpoints but if Chanler cut-points were express in ActiGraphy counts then see:
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/CutPoints.html#cut-points-not-expressed-in-gravitational-units-not-in-this-vignette
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#do-neishabouricounts

Note that cut-points are specified differently for GGIR part 2 and 5:
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter11_DescribingDataCutPoints.html

Best wishes,

Vincent
